description: Directory names never traversed during discovery, and the names deliberately traversed despite looking skippable. Names, not paths: a name is portable across machines, a path is not. Replace or extend with CODESS_DISCOVERY_POLICY.

traversed_on_purpose.conf: checked-in configuration, under a second spelling
traversed_on_purpose.credentials: pruning is not a security control; see security_note
traversed_on_purpose.data: fixtures, migrations, and seed files are versioned source
traversed_on_purpose.etc: checked-in configuration in many server projects
traversed_on_purpose.lib: a library's own source in C, Ruby, and Node layouts
traversed_on_purpose.private: access intent, not content kind: private source is still source
traversed_on_purpose.public: the served root of a web project, usually versioned
traversed_on_purpose.secrets: pruning is not a security control; see security_note
traversed_on_purpose.static: the served root, under a second spelling
traversed_on_purpose.web: the front-end half of a full-stack repository
traversed_on_purpose.windows: a platform port directory, not build output

security_note: Pruning stops traversal, which changes what is discovered rather than what is protected. A Session that already read a credential file records it whether or not Codess later walks that directory. Content exclusion is the content policy's subject. A name-based skip that looked like protection would be worse than none, because it invites trusting it.
editing_note: Add a name to a pruned group when your tree has a directory of that kind that is generated or transient. Move a name out of traversed_on_purpose only for your own tree: each is a source directory in a common layout, so pruning it hides the Project rather than the noise.
